segments.text: A table scan tests rows to find matching data. An index maps keys to rows and can find matching entries without testing every row. An index takes storage space and must be updated when indexed values change.

draft.objective: Compare scanning with an index lookup

narration_units.text: Imagine finding a matching value in an illustrative table. A table scan tests candidate rows against the search condition.
Without a useful index, the scan can examine many rows before finding a match.

narration_units.purpose: Replace scanning with a lookup mechanism
narration_units.text: An index instead maps a search key to matching rows, so the lookup need not test every row.
That shortcut has a trade-off: the index needs storage and updates when indexed values change.

scenes.summary: Illustrative table scan from candidate to match
Index points to a row with maintenance cost
